Title: Nacho Vigalondo: 'Me parece demencial que nadie en su sano juicio cuestione un videojuego por tener un precio accesible'

Summary: 
Nacho Vigalondo, the Spanish filmmaker born in 1977, discusses his new documentary "Tribute"—set to stream on Prime Video on 11 September—about the history of video games in Spain. The film follows his childhood memories of a boy named Pindorro who played in local recreation centers and traces the evolution of the industry to the rise of e‑sports and influential streamers such as Illo Juan. Vigalondo, together with writer Rubén Ajaú and Domino’s Pizza, interviewed at the Museo del Videojuego de Madrid, talks about the common phobia of olives and the difference between hatred and phobia. He criticises the tendency to divide fans over consoles, comparing it to the Marvel vs. DC debate, and explains that he used to defend the Mega Drive in school but now sees no reason to favour one console over another. The interview covers the shift from hobby magazines like Hobby Consolas to watching gameplays, and Vigalondo’s view that masterpieces in gaming—such as the first three Resident Evil titles, The Last of Us, and Grand Theft Auto—pre‑exist before mainstream recognition. He also comments on the price of games, arguing that a low price for a well‑made title like "Silksong" (priced at 20 euros) should not be questioned. Vigalondo says, 'Me parece demencial que nadie en su sano juicio cuestione un videojuego por tener un precio accesible.' He concludes that while he would consider adapting a game to film, he believes a good game does not need a movie. The article was published on 12 September 2025 by El HuffPost.

Title: El retraso de GTA VI sacude a la industria de videojuegos: pérdidas y expectativas récord

Summary: 
The announcement that Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) will now launch on 26 May 2026, instead of 2025, has sent shockwaves through the video‑game industry.  Take‑Two Interactive’s shares fell almost 10 % immediately after the news, and analysts at Ampere Analysis estimate that the delay could cost the industry up to $2.7 billion in 2025 revenue that would otherwise have been generated.  The impact is underscored by the legacy of GTA V, which sold more than 215 million copies worldwide and generated roughly $9 billion in revenue, making it the most profitable entertainment product of its generation.  GTA V’s business model—continuous income from GTA Online micro‑transactions and downloadable content—has set a benchmark that investors expect Rockstar to replicate and expand in GTA VI.  Consequently, analysts predict a significant boost in PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S sales in 2026, especially in the U.S. and Europe, as both Sony and Microsoft have recently raised console prices in anticipation of higher demand.  One of the most discussed aspects is the rumored $100 price tag for the standard edition, a figure that Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take‑Two, described as ‘justo’ and in line with the product’s value, though the final price remains unconfirmed.  While no official confirmation exists for in‑game real‑money systems akin to Roblox, a stronger digital economy is expected in GTA Online 2, with a focus on micro‑transactions and experience customization.  The industry’s future hinges on GTA VI maintaining recurring revenue streams beyond its initial launch.  The game’s pre‑sales, console‑driving potential, and financial impact make it a watershed moment for global entertainment.  The ‘GTA effect’ has already prompted publishers such as Electronic Arts, Ubisoft, and Capcom to adjust release calendars to avoid direct competition.  In December 2023, the second GTA VI trailer amassed 475 million views in 24 hours—a record that eclipsed major film releases like *Deadpool & Wolverine* and *Avengers: Endgame*, underscoring the cultural and commercial phenomenon that the launch is expected to become.

Published date: September 01 2025, 16:13
